msgs.text: Hi Jonny, thanks for hopping on. This chat will take about two or three minutes so our team can hear it in your own words. What problem are you hoping to solve or what opportunity are you chasing?
I don't know what to do
Thanks for saying that, it's useful to know. So,
... Maybe we wa- we, maybe we want to make a new app which is about... ... travel to China, something like that
Hmm. A travel app for China. What is it that made this feel like a priority now? Was it, you know, business strategy, a recent event, new research, what brought it up?
Okay. That's useful to know too. Who would this affect most? You know, who are the customers or people right at the centre of it?
I think for outside of China, the foreigners
Yeah, foreigners. Well, have you already tried anything in that area or is this pretty much brand new?
Mm. With that in mind, if it all goes well, what does success look like for you over the longer term? I just mean in plain terms, not numbers.
Maybe 100 million new regist-registered users, I think, or uh, daily user activity- daily user... upset visit, something like that

Right, so strong usage and engagement. And for the workshop itself, what would you like to leave with? You could think of an example like a prototype, or a direction tested with users, or a decision about what to pursue.
Uh... one prototype. Proto, I think
A prototype. Is there a business you think already does some part of this really well? Or you can skip it if you don't have an example.
Thanks, Jonny. That gives us enough to work from for now. I'll play back what I've heard on the next screen. When you're ready, please press the red phone button to end the call.

alts.headline: XYZ Company backs China travel app after testing demand
alts.body: The app gives people outside China one place to plan trips to China, helping foreign visitors return for travel needs. Testing showed enough demand and regular use for XYZ Company to invest further before building at scale.
alts.quote: We now have evidence that people want this, not just an idea we hoped would work.
alts.photo: Foreign travellers compare phones and paper maps in a busy Chinese railway station, planning their next stop in natural afternoon light. The image is candid, with nobody looking at the camera and no visible text, logos or brand names.

runsheet.p: Agree that the first decision is whether this idea deserves further investment. Set aside the 100 million user ambition until the team has clearer evidence of a real planning problem.

Find out how people outside China currently plan a China trip, where planning breaks down, and which tasks they would want in one place. Separate needs for first-time visitors from needs for people who travel to China regularly.
Turn the strongest planning need into a simple One Trip Plan or Ready To Go prototype. Keep the prototype narrow enough to test the core value of making a China trip easier to plan.
Put the prototype in front of people outside China who are planning, or have recently planned, a China trip. Check whether they understand it, use it to plan, and would return to it.
Agree what evidence would support more investment, what would stop it, and who will make that decision. Set the next learning step so the team does not spend time building before the need is clear.

cut: The target audience is people outside China who want to travel to China.
The intended customer change is planning a China trip in one place.
The challenge is how to make China travel planning easier for this audience.
Growing users, building regular usage, and testing further investment are already ranked as business goals.

gaps.p: The brief does not name who will decide whether the app deserves further investment. Confirm the person or group who owns that call.
The brief does not say what currently makes China travel planning hard. Find the specific tasks, gaps, and frustrations the prototype must address.
People outside China is a broad group. Agree which travellers to test first, such as people planning their first China trip or people travelling soon.
The brief does not define regular usage or what would support the 100 million user ambition. Set practical signs of need and usage to check before more investment.
